stories.headline: Taiwan panel makers and Corning target glass-based advanced packaging
bullets: Innolux and AUO are developing panel-level packaging and glass-based optical-interconnect solutions with Corning as AI demand raises the need for larger, lower-loss packages.
Innolux is reported to be developing glass optical-channel coupling components for co-packaged optics, while AUO is developing a system-level Micro LED CPO module.
The companies are positioning glass substrates, RDL and panel-scale manufacturing for AI, HPC and high-speed optical interconnects, including potential cooperation with TSMC.
stories.topic: Foundry · Compute · Advanced Packaging · Substrates · Supply Chain
stories.score_reason: Glass substrates, panel-level packaging and co-packaged optics are strategically important responses to AI interconnect and package-size constraints.

stories.headline: SK E&S plans to expand South Korean offshore wind capacity toward 900MW
bullets: SK E&S and Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners operate the 96MW Jeonnam 1 offshore wind farm, which sources about 75% of major equipment and installation services from South Korean companies.
The partners plan to build the 399MW Jeonnam 2 and 399MW Jeonnam 3 projects from 2028, targeting about 900MW of total capacity by 2031.
SK E&S said the projects could help supply renewable power for future semiconductor factories in the region.
stories.score_reason: The planned renewable-power buildout is relevant to future semiconductor-factory power availability and local industrial supply chains.

stories.headline: Shanghai Jiao Tong team reports progress on heterogeneously integrated electro-optic modulators
bullets: Jiwei reposts a Shanghai Jiao Tong University announcement describing progress in micro-transfer heterogeneously integrated electro-optic modulators.
The work involved teams from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University and Huazhong University of Science and Technology.
stories.score_reason: Relevant heterogeneous-integration research with possible photonics-packaging significance, although the supplied repost is truncated.

bullets: Senators Bernie Sanders and Greg Cezar announced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, according to Tom’s Hardware.
The proposal would threaten rule breakers with prison sentences of up to 20 years.
The bill would regulate developers who proceed with artificial-superintelligence plans.
stories.score_reason: The proposal represents a potentially consequential US policy response to frontier-AI development, though it is only a legislative proposal.

stories.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI debate slowing frontier-AI development for safety
bullets: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for AI development to slow so safety and alignment measures can catch up, warning that an AI-agent swarm could take over the internet within six to 12 months.

AP reported that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman committed to one of Amodei’s safety proposals; the Ijiwei recap describes temporary restrictions on some OpenAI training and research activity after agent-security incidents.

The proposals include stronger external assessment, common safety standards and limited international coordination; the supplied claims about incidents and future risks remain attributed rather than independently verified.
stories.score_reason: This is a major frontier-AI pacing and safety development involving two leading labs, concrete governance proposals and warnings about autonomous agents.

stories.headline: Sigmaintell sees OLED TV shipments peaking in 2028 as memory costs rise
bullets: Sigmaintell forecasts global OLED TV shipments will rise from 6.1 million units in 2024 to 7.6 million in 2028 before declining in 2029 and 2030.
The research firm said memory’s share of manufacturing cost for a 65-inch TV could reach 20–21% from the third quarter of 2026 through the second quarter of 2027.
For 32-inch TVs, memory’s cost share was forecast to rise to 41–44%, while AUO’s possible LCD-panel exit could contribute to supply tightness from 2028.
stories.score_reason: The research links consumer-display demand with rapidly rising memory cost exposure and possible future panel supply tightness.

stories.headline: Z.ai seeks another roughly US$5 billion from equity and convertible debt
bullets: SCMP reports that Z.ai, also known as Zhipu AI, is seeking about US$2 billion through a Hong Kong share placement and another US$3 billion through convertible bonds.
The company is also pursuing a potential Shanghai Star Market listing, although no application had been publicly accepted in the supplied report.
The fundraising highlights the capital intensity of developing frontier AI models.
stories.score_reason: A potential US$5 billion capital raise by a Chinese frontier-model developer is a major model-economics and funding event.

stories.headline: Shanghai Jiao Tong team demonstrates a broadband heterogeneous photonic modulator
bullets: The team combined thin-film lithium tantalate with silicon nitride using micro-transfer printing to build a Mach–Zehnder electro-optic modulator.
Tests across 42 devices showed average insertion loss of about 0.8dB, average extinction ratio of about 28.6dB and an electro-optic bandwidth of roughly 110GHz.
Demonstrations included 375Gbps PAM8 optical transmission, 148Gbps D-band wireless transmission and millimetre-scale radar ranging.

companies.name: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

stories.score_reason: The research demonstrates heterogeneous photonic integration with high-speed optical and wireless applications relevant to future interconnects.

stories.headline: Shanghai Jiao Tong team leads a RISC-V security extension into the ISA standard
bullets: Ijiwei reported that the RISC-V International board approved the SPMP privileged physical-memory-protection extension on August 31.
The Shanghai Jiao Tong IPADS team led the proposal from its 2019 submission through nearly seven years of review and standardisation.
SPMP uses lightweight physical-region checks for security isolation and has reportedly been deployed in the XiangShan processor and Xinlai RISC-V IP.
stories.score_reason: A China-led contribution to an international processor standard is strategically relevant to RISC-V security and the broader processor ecosystem.

stories.headline: Researchers propose engineering benchmarks for deployable optical computing
bullets: Shanghai Jiao Tong and Tsinghua researchers published a framework intended to move optical computing beyond isolated laboratory demonstrations toward manufacturable, programmable and scalable systems.
The framework compares architectures across compute scale, precision, energy efficiency and programmability for AI, edge and scientific-computing workloads.
The team proposed quantitative targets, including more than 22dB extinction ratio and specified loss limits for scaling optical matrix operations beyond 64×64.
stories.score_reason: The work provides engineering criteria for assessing whether optical computing can progress from prototypes to deployable AI and scientific-computing systems.

stories.headline: Researchers develop a VO2 temperature-threshold protection device for integrated chips
bullets: A Hangzhou Dianzi University team used vanadium dioxide’s sharp metal–insulator transition to build a temperature-threshold diode that can rapidly divert abnormal current.
The device changes resistance by two to three orders of magnitude within a temperature range narrower than 5°C, according to the report.
Three-dimensional integration with through-silicon vias was demonstrated for semiconductor-bridge protection and potential chip-level thermal management.
stories.score_reason: The work proposes a distinct protection device for high-reliability integrated circuits and extreme-environment systems.

stories.headline: Researchers demonstrate long-term stable on-chip optical-comb locking
bullets: A National University of Defense Technology team developed a multimodal-locking architecture for a silicon-nitride microcomb source.
The report said the system achieved long-duration full-lock stability in complex environments, with repetition-rate stability at the reported 10^-14-per-10,000-second level.
Potential applications include micrometre-scale inter-satellite ranging and femtosecond time-frequency transfer.
stories.score_reason: Stable integrated frequency-comb operation is relevant to photonic-chip timing, precision measurement and satellite links.

stories.headline: MoXin Technology reportedly seeks a new RMB1 billion financing round for its world model
bullets: Ijiwei reported that Hangzhou-based MoXin Technology may complete a financing round of about RMB1 billion at a valuation near RMB10 billion.
The company’s MoWorld 4D model was reportedly trained, compressed and deployed on domestic NPUs, with real-time inference of about 50 frames per second.
The model is being explored for industrial digital twins, embodied-AI training, urban planning and immersive content.
stories.topic: Compute · Models · China Models · China Supply Chain
stories.score_reason: The reported financing and domestic-NPU deployment connect model economics, Chinese AI infrastructure and industrial applications, though the round is not confirmed.

stories.headline: Tuobang signs a master supply agreement with Vertiv
bullets: Tuobang will supply Vertiv with PCBA, electronic components, electromechanical components and system assemblies for UPS power equipment.
The framework agreement leaves product models, quantities, prices and delivery schedules to later orders.
Ijiwei reported that transactions between the companies since the start of 2026 totaled about RMB28.8 million, while future volumes remain uncertain.
stories.score_reason: The agreement expands a component supplier’s role in data-center power infrastructure, though execution and volume remain uncertain.

stories.headline: TrendForce sees record second-quarter foundry revenue
bullets: TrendForce said the world’s ten largest foundries were expected to generate $53.49 billion in second-quarter output, up 11.5% sequentially.
The report attributed the record growth to strong demand for AI high-performance-computing chips and related integrated circuits, with consumer-electronics pre-stocking also contributing.
The roundup said SMIC revenue grew 20%.
stories.score_reason: TrendForce research directly addresses global foundry capacity and revenue, with AI demand driving a record market level.

stories.headline: Inspur seeks up to RMB9 billion for AI infrastructure expansion
bullets: Inspur plans a private placement of up to RMB9 billion, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.
Proposed projects include AI infrastructure for large-scale agent applications, liquid-cooled green computing clusters and multi-agent storage-compute integration.
Funds would also support high-density computing equipment manufacturing and working capital.
stories.topic: Compute · China Supply Chain · Supply Chain
stories.score_reason: The proposed financing is large and specifically targets AI infrastructure, liquid cooling and high-density computing equipment.

stories.headline: Jianghua Micro and Shanghai Chemical Research Institute agree on electronic-chemical R&D
bullets: Jianghua Micro and Shanghai Chemical Research Institute signed a five-year strategic cooperation framework.
The work will target purification, impurity control, analysis and stability of ultra-high-purity electronic chemicals for semiconductor and display applications.
The companies also plan a joint laboratory, shared intellectual-property work, talent development and supply-chain cooperation.
stories.score_reason: The agreement addresses domestic supply and process development for high-purity semiconductor chemicals, a key materials bottleneck.

stories.headline: Shantou Ultrasonic Electronics denies Nvidia-supply rumour
bullets: Shantou Ultrasonic Electronics said a market rumour that its high-frequency PCB had received Nvidia certification was untrue and that it currently supplies no products to Nvidia.
Its 800G and 1.6T optical-module supporting PCBs remain in research and development, with customer certification, mass production and revenue still uncertain.
The company said its recent share-price volatility did not reflect a material change in its fundamentals.
stories.score_reason: The clarification addresses a market-moving AI-hardware supply claim and distinguishes development work from actual Nvidia shipments.

stories.headline: Anthropic alleges China-linked military, surveillance and distillation use of Claude
bullets: Anthropic’s September threat report, as recapped by Tom’s Hardware, alleges that China-linked actors used Claude for an anti-torpedo specification and software modules for electronic-warfare and air-defence suppression.
The report also describes surveillance activity targeting Uyghur groups and diaspora activists, using Claude to process communications and map social networks.

Anthropic alleged that Alibaba-linked operators generated more than 151 million Claude exchanges while attempting to distil capabilities into Qwen models; the claims were not independently verified in the supplied coverage.
stories.score_reason: The allegations concern frontier-model misuse, military applications and industrial-scale distillation involving major Chinese AI actors; attribution and uncertainty are preserved.

stories.headline: Espressif’s ESP32-P4 runs a playable 3D game at about 1 watt
bullets: Tom’s Hardware reported that a sub-$25 development board using Espressif’s dual-core 400MHz ESP32-P4 ran OpenLara at 320×240 resolution and scaled it to a 1,024×600 display.
The microcontroller uses RISC-V cores with AI instruction extensions, up to 64MB of PSRAM, 768KB of SRAM, an FPU, DSP and ISP.
The demonstration consumed roughly 1 watt at peak and included stereo audio and USB-keyboard control.
stories.score_reason: A concrete low-power microcontroller demonstration illustrates expanding embedded compute capability, although its commercial impact is limited.

stories.headline: Chinese researchers report a 100-fold endurance gain for ferroelectric memory
bullets: Researchers from Xidian University, City University of Hong Kong and Fudan University demonstrated more than 10 billion writing cycles in wurtzite ferroelectrics, according to SCMP.
The work targets aluminium scandium nitride, or AlScN, a potential next-generation memory material with fast switching and low-power characteristics.
The research was published in Science and could move the material closer to practical high-performance-computing and AI memory applications.
stories.score_reason: Substantive materials advance addressing a major reliability barrier for emerging memory used in future AI and HPC systems.

stories.headline: SK says its AWS-linked Ulsan AI data center could reach 1GW
bullets: SK is developing an AI data center in Ulsan with Amazon Web Services, with reported investment of about 7 trillion won.
SK Chairman Chey Tae-won said discussions had progressed toward adding 900MW to an initial roughly 100MW buildout, bringing the potential scale to about 1GW.
Chey argued that AI investment needs sustainable business models, data platforms and recurring returns.
stories.score_reason: A potential 1GW AI datacenter is a major compute-infrastructure and power-demand development, with explicit implications for AI economics.

stories.headline: Hyundai Research Institute raises South Korea’s 2026 growth forecast on semiconductor strength
bullets: Hyundai Research Institute raised its 2026 South Korean growth forecast from 2.7% to 3.5%, citing AI investment and strong semiconductor exports.
The institute expects 2027 growth to slow to 2.4% as base effects and weaker domestic demand offset continued semiconductor-led exports.
It warned that weaker AI investment or stronger competition from Chinese memory suppliers could cause a sharper export slowdown.
stories.score_reason: Macroeconomic research directly links South Korea’s growth outlook to semiconductor exports, AI investment and memory competition.

stories.headline: South Korea launches an AI-datacenter multicore-fibre interconnect programme
bullets: South Korea’s science ministry is seeking companies and research institutes for spatial-division-multiplexed optical interfaces using multicore fibre for AI data centers.
The project could run through 2031 and has total government support of 3.6 billion won.
The programme targets the bandwidth and power limitations of copper connections as AI data centers scale to tens of thousands of GPUs.

companies.name: South Korean Ministry of Science and ICT

stories.topic: Compute · Advanced Packaging · Materials & Inputs · Supply Chain
stories.score_reason: The programme targets optical interconnect capacity, a growing bottleneck as AI clusters scale beyond conventional electrical links.

stories.headline: Hyundai targets its own Atria AI autonomy platform for 2029 production
bullets: Hyundai Motor Group plans Nvidia-based Level 2+ driving functions in mass-production vehicles in the first half of 2028 and Level 2++ functions later that year.
The group targets mass production of vehicles using its own Atria AI platform for Level 2++ functions in the second half of 2029, after further testing and safety development.

Hyundai is also developing a vision-language-action model and says its data-flywheel strategy will use production-vehicle data to improve models, with a goal of surpassing leading competitors’ cumulative driving data by 2033.
stories.score_reason: The combined media-day disclosures cover a major automaker’s autonomy roadmap, AI model development, sensor standardisation and large-scale data strategy.

stories.headline: Chinese project combines domestic GPUs and neuromorphic chips for AI inference
bullets: Mobile Cloud and research partners released what they described as China’s first heterogeneous large-model inference system combining domestic GPUs with neuromorphic chips.
In reported DeepSeek V4 testing, the system achieved more than twice the cost performance of a comparable domestic-GPU cluster and cut operating costs by more than 40%.
The architecture assigns attention workloads to GPUs and latency-sensitive FFN/MOE workloads to neuromorphic chips through a compiler, interconnect and unified inference engine.
stories.topic: Compute · Models · China Models · China Supply Chain
stories.score_reason: The system proposes a differentiated domestic-accelerator architecture for reducing inference cost and improving heterogeneous-chip utilisation.

stories.headline: Yongin and UNIST launch a semiconductor and AI executive programme
bullets: Yongin and UNIST began a 14-week programme for executives from seven semiconductor materials, parts and equipment companies.
The curriculum covers logic, memory, HBM, advanced packaging, semiconductor equipment and AI-sector strategy.
The programme is intended to strengthen local industry-academic cooperation in Yongin’s semiconductor cluster.

companies.name: UNIST
aliases: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

stories.topic: WFE · Foundry · DRAM · Advanced Packaging · Supply Chain
stories.score_reason: The programme is a smaller workforce and ecosystem development event, but it directly targets HBM, packaging and semiconductor suppliers.

stories.headline: South Korea broadens espionage law to protect semiconductor know-how
bullets: South Korea’s amended Criminal Act took effect on September 13, extending espionage provisions from conduct benefiting North Korea to activity conducted for any foreign country or equivalent organisation.
The new offence carries a minimum three-year prison sentence and is intended to protect semiconductors, displays, batteries and artificial intelligence technology.
The change follows a case involving former Samsung Electronics employees accused of transferring DRAM technology to China’s ChangXin Storage.
stories.score_reason: The law materially changes technology-protection and industrial-espionage risk for Korea’s strategic semiconductor sector.

stories.headline: OpenAI’s reported mathematics result draws criticism from leading mathematicians
bullets: Hankook Ilbo reports that OpenAI announced an AI-generated solution to the long-standing Navier–Stokes problem.

Twenty-five Fields Medal winners criticized the use of difficult mathematical problems as AI performance benchmarks, arguing that proof development and peer verification are central to mathematical research.
The supplied report says the result had not been recognized as an official solution by the Clay Mathematics Institute.
stories.score_reason: Material frontier-model capability and verification dispute involving prominent mathematicians and a major AI lab.

stories.headline: AI-coding tools continue rapid growth and consolidation
bullets: Ijiwei cited one estimate putting the global AI-coding-tools market at $29.57 billion in 2025 and $64.68 billion in 2030, while noting that other estimates differ materially.
The analysis describes Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor and Devin as leading products and argues that standalone tools are increasingly being absorbed by companies with large-scale compute.
It also says cloud and local deployment are converging, while compute subsidies, model dependence and code-quality and security review remain risks.
stories.score_reason: The report addresses frontier-model economics, AI-agent commercialisation and consolidation of developer tools around compute owners.

stories.headline: AI datacenter growth accelerates North American ESS demand
bullets: US commercial and industrial ESS installations reached a record 1.8GWh in the second quarter, with another roughly 6GWh expected in the second half, according to the supplied market summary.
AI datacenters are increasing demand for storage systems able to provide more than 10 hours of power.
LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI and SK On are expanding North American ESS production or supply agreements, with non-China sourcing gaining importance.
stories.score_reason: AI power demand is creating a significant adjacent market for batteries, grid storage and long-duration power systems.

stories.headline: Material Science validates a PFAS-free low-index OLED capping layer
bullets: Material Science said it completed mass-production process validation for a low-refractive-index capping layer targeting mobile and tablet OLED panels.
The material reportedly achieved a refractive index below 1.5 and optical absorption of k=0.00 while avoiding PFAS compounds.
The company also said it validated thermal stability and resistance to deposition-nozzle clogging, two barriers to production-line adoption.
stories.score_reason: The development addresses OLED efficiency, production reliability and future chemical-regulation constraints, though the company is not identified as a major public supplier.

stories.headline: KT and Amlogic sign an MOU to secure media-chip supplies
bullets: KT and US fabless chip designer Amlogic signed an MOU for a more stable supply chain for key chips used in KT media terminals.
The companies have previously worked together on 8K Android TV set-top boxes and plan to continue cooperation on SoC supply and AI functions.
KT said the arrangement is intended to reduce global semiconductor-supply risk and improve continuity of media services.
stories.score_reason: The agreement directly addresses media-device chip supply continuity and adds future AI-SoC cooperation between a major operator and fabless supplier.

stories.headline: Vietnam says semiconductor talent supply meets only about 20% of need
bullets: Vietnam will need at least 50,000 university-educated semiconductor workers by 2030, while current supply meets only about 20% of practical demand, according to the report.
The largest gaps remain in manufacturing, packaging, testing and research, where training is described as too theoretical and practical facilities and experienced instructors are limited.
Universities are expanding company-linked programmes and factory internships, including cooperation connected with Samsung’s production ecosystem.
stories.score_reason: Workforce shortages could constrain Vietnam’s ability to capture semiconductor design, manufacturing, packaging and testing investment.

stories.headline: US robot-import rules threaten Korean AI-hardware exports
bullets: ETNews reports that US restrictions on foreign advanced robots are creating export and certification risks for Korean companies.
Exemptions reportedly require US manufacturing and at least 65% US content in the parts supply chain, while conditional approval requires extensive ownership and BOM disclosures.
Korean industry groups are seeking government support for certification, supply-chain documentation and negotiations with US authorities.
stories.score_reason: The reported rules could materially reshape Korean AI-robot hardware supply chains and exports to the US, although the detailed requirements remain attributed to industry coverage.

stories.headline: China’s Empyrean Technology applies agentic AI to EDA workflows
bullets: Empyrean Technology chairman Liu Weiping said an AI agent integrated with simulation and layout tools cut a circuit-layout task from four weeks to one week.
The company is developing an agentic EDA platform in which its tools can work with partners’ agents.
Liu said the business model could shift from conventional software licences toward token consumption for agentic EDA.
stories.score_reason: AI-assisted EDA is directly relevant to China’s chip-design self-sufficiency and could materially change design productivity and software economics.

stories.headline: California passes new child-safety rules for AI chatbots and social platforms
bullets: California passed legislation requiring AI services to conduct independent child-safety audits before launch and annual risk assessments, according to Hankook Ilbo.
AI chatbots would have to trigger emergency procedures and notify parents or guardians when they detect self-harm or suicide risk in a minor’s conversation.
The package also restricts infinite scrolling, autoplay and behavioural recommendations for users under 16; the report said legal challenges are possible.
stories.score_reason: The package is a significant state-level AI safety and platform-regulation development affecting model deployment and child protections.

stories.headline: KT outlines a national AI service linking 16 companies and domestic models
bullets: KT’s consortium for South Korea’s government-backed ‘AI for Everyone’ initiative includes Upstage, Motif Technologies, Saltlux, NC AI, Rebellions and multiple consumer-service companies.
The consortium plans to connect AI features across services reaching more than 60 million user touchpoints.
KT said its Token Factory platform will route different domestic models to tasks such as reasoning, long-context processing, 3D and sound generation.
stories.score_reason: The project is a substantial national-scale AI deployment and domestic-model integration initiative with broad service reach.

stories.headline: Micron Taiwan junior engineers reportedly receive average bonuses of NT$720,000
bullets: Xinzhixun posts an article saying Micron paid Taiwan junior engineers an average bonus of NT$720,000.
The supplied text does not state the payment period or the number of employees covered.
stories.score_reason: Material semiconductor labor-cost and retention news involving a major memory company, though the supplied evidence is limited to an article headline.

stories.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity remains undersupplied, report says
bullets: Xinzhixun reports that TSMC's CoWoS capacity remains in short supply.
The article says Amkor, UMC and ASE could benefit from the constraint.
stories.score_reason: CoWoS is a critical AI-packaging bottleneck, and the report identifies multiple potential capacity beneficiaries.

stories.headline: Lam Research sees AI equipment supercycle constrained by cleanrooms
bullets: Lam Research CFO Douglas Bettinger said semiconductor demand is extremely strong and that cleanroom capacity, rather than demand, is the main constraint.
Lam expects its largest customer to bring 8 to 10 new cleanrooms online from now through the end of next year and is prioritising delivery, hiring and supply-chain execution.
DRAM leads current capital spending, followed by advanced logic, while NAND investment is expected to shift toward new greenfield projects.
stories.topic: WFE · Compute · DRAM · NAND · Supply Chain
stories.score_reason: A leading equipment supplier identifies cleanroom capacity as the bottleneck in an AI-led semiconductor expansion cycle and gives a concrete customer buildout outlook.

stories.headline: Murata reallocates MLCC capacity toward AI servers
bullets: Murata is discontinuing some specifications across nine MLCC series, with final orders due in March 2028 and final shipments in March 2029.
The move is attributed to production being redirected toward higher-value AI-server MLCCs, which require substantially more manufacturing resources than general-purpose parts.
Distributor inventories were reported down 8% over four weeks while unit prices rose 7%; Samsung Electro-Mechanics was cited as a potential beneficiary.
stories.score_reason: A major passive-component supplier is reallocating capacity away from general-purpose products, signalling tightening AI-server component supply.

stories.headline: Hanwha Ocean unveils a modular 60MW floating AI datacenter design
bullets: Hanwha Ocean plans to show a physical model of a 60MW floating data center at Gastech 2026, its first public display of the concept.
The design is modular, allowing power generation, server type, capacity and installation configuration to be adjusted to customer and site requirements.
The company said the concept has received basic certification for its design from the American Bureau of Shipping.
stories.score_reason: The project is a material alternative datacenter architecture aimed at overcoming land, power and cooling constraints.

stories.headline: AI-interconnect chip designer Netforward completes A-share IPO guidance
bullets: Netforward completed its initial-public-offering guidance process and is advancing toward a proposed A-share listing, according to the report.
The company designs Ethernet switching, smart-NIC, PHY and PCIe-switch products; its 100G/400G data-center switch chips have reportedly exceeded 400,000 units shipped.
Its AI-interconnect roadmap includes PCIe 6.0, CXL, UALink and planned 400G/800G smart-NIC products for large AI clusters.
stories.score_reason: The proposed listing and expansion from networking silicon into PCIe, CXL, UALink and high-speed AI-cluster interconnects make this a relevant domestic-chip development.

stories.headline: US-China model-distillation dispute moves into government-level AI policy
bullets: The report said the NSA, FBI and CISA accused DeepSeek, Moonshot, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun and Z.AI of using industrial-scale distillation to obtain capabilities from US frontier models.

China’s Ministry of Commerce rejected the allegations, arguing that distillation is widely used and that the real issue is whether model outputs were obtained without authorisation or at systematic scale.
The dispute could lead to tighter controls on models, chips and cloud access, while the report described possible limited cooperation on AI safety testing and crisis communications.
stories.score_reason: The supplied report describes an escalation from corporate accusations to US national-security agencies and Chinese government response, with potential consequences for AI and semiconductor controls.

stories.headline: South Korean semiconductor exports continue to drive record trade growth
bullets: South Korea’s exports reached US$728.6 billion by September 10, up 54.1% year over year, according to customs data cited by Asia Economy.
August semiconductor exports reached a record US$46.65 billion, up 209%, while September 1–10 semiconductor exports rose 270.1% year over year.
Semiconductors accounted for 47.1% of exports in the first ten days of September, as AI-infrastructure demand supported memory and enterprise-SSD components.
stories.score_reason: The figures show an unusually large semiconductor contribution to national trade and continuing AI-driven memory demand.

stories.headline: Global server revenue hit a record $166.3 billion in Q2
bullets: IDC reported second-quarter global server revenue of $166.3 billion, up 52% year over year and 35.7% sequentially, as AI infrastructure investment lifted both shipments and average system prices.
GPU-server revenue reached $87.4 billion despite a reported 10.8% shipment decline, while other accelerated-server revenue rose 237.6% to $27.5 billion.
DRAM and NAND pricing, component shortages, power, cooling and facility readiness were all identified as constraints; Lenovo also reached first place in global x86 server unit shipments.
stories.score_reason: The reported record market size and sharp price increases show AI infrastructure demand broadening into mainstream servers while component and facility constraints intensify.

stories.headline: Samsung Display to supply newer M16 OLED materials for Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra
bullets: Samsung Electronics and Samsung Display are reported to have selected the newer M16 material set for Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra OLED panels.
The standard Galaxy S27 and S27 Plus are expected to move from M13 to M14, creating a materials distinction between the ranges.
Samsung Display is reported to supply all OLED panels for the Galaxy S27 lineup planned for release in the first quarter of next year.
stories.score_reason: The report describes a meaningful OLED-material generation change and supplier allocation for a major smartphone product line.

stories.headline: South Korean supply chains increasingly use connector countries between the US and China
bullets: A Bank of Korea analysis says Vietnam and other ASEAN countries have become intermediary production hubs linking Korean supply chains to both US and Chinese demand.
For Korean computer, electronics and optical-equipment exports, the share routed through ASEAN countries rose above the China-transit share by 2022.
The analysis warns that stronger US origin and circumvention rules could increase risks and recommends reducing dependence on any single production route.
stories.score_reason: The research directly addresses geopolitical restructuring of semiconductor-related production routes and the resilience risks of connector-country dependence.

stories.headline: Lotte and KAIST open an R&D center targeting AI-chip materials
bullets: Lotte and KAIST opened a 4,298-square-metre R&D center funded partly by a 10 billion won Lotte construction donation.

Lotte Chemical plans to research AI-semiconductor and low-earth-orbit satellite-communications materials, while Lotte Energy Materials will develop high-speed transmission-circuit materials for data centers and AI accelerators.
The center is intended to cover basic research, experiments, prototyping and technology commercialisation in one location.
stories.score_reason: New institutional R&D capacity targets AI-chip materials and high-speed interconnect inputs used in datacenter infrastructure.

stories.headline: LG Display expands its company-wide AX Squad
bullets: LG Display says employees across manufacturing, development and administrative functions are creating AI projects with coaching from internal AI specialists.
The programme has accumulated more than 450 projects, including about 190 automated tasks such as defect classification, optical simulation and employee surveys.
The company is extending the programme into procurement, supply chain, customer support, finance, management, sales and marketing.
stories.score_reason: The initiative shows a major display manufacturer embedding AI development across production and supply-chain functions, with reported measurable adoption.

stories.headline: US and China pursue AI systems that help build better AI
bullets: SCMP reports that leading US and Chinese AI companies are using models to write code, design experiments and develop training methods for more capable successors.
OpenAI has described a goal of building an automated AI researcher but said it remains uncertain how to make recursive self-improvement safe and aligned.
Z.ai founder Tang Jie said the company’s next-generation GLM-6 was moving toward self-evolution, according to the report.
stories.score_reason: The story covers a material frontier-AI development direction—models contributing to the development of successor models—with explicit safety uncertainty.

stories.headline: Jukan proposes an AI arms-control framework
bullets: Jukan argues that the United States and China should consider an AI version of the Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty.
He says unilateral US restraint would be ineffective if China does not also slow down.
stories.score_reason: The post is a relevant attributed policy view on reciprocal frontier-AI pacing and international coordination, rather than a reported development.

stories.headline: Dell’Oro: AI data-center semiconductor and component revenue surged 182%
bullets: Dell’Oro reported that suppliers of semiconductors and components for global data-center servers and storage recorded 182% year-over-year revenue growth in the second quarter.
DRAM and storage-drive revenue both grew by triple digits, while average selling prices per bit more than doubled from a year earlier.
Demand expanded from accelerators to HBM, CPUs, high-speed networking, storage and general-purpose servers; supply constraints could restrict hyperscaler infrastructure plans.
stories.score_reason: Material industry research indicates a sharp expansion in AI-linked semiconductor and component demand, with pricing and supply constraints affecting the broader datacenter market.

stories.headline: Chey proposes giving AI agents to Ulsan’s roughly one million residents
bullets: SK Chairman Chey Tae-won proposed providing Ulsan residents with AI agents covering public benefits, daily information, administration, transport, healthcare and education.
He said personal data could be protected through coding or other privacy controls and combined with manufacturing data to improve city services.
Chey framed the proposal as part of an ‘AI City’ model that combines manufacturing, public AI and sustainable business models.
stories.score_reason: Material public-sector AI deployment proposal from a major Korean industrial group, tied to data infrastructure and manufacturing AI.

stories.headline: Qualcomm unveils a new Hexagon NPU for on-device agentic AI
bullets: Qualcomm’s next-generation Hexagon NPU adds an Element Accelerator, 50% more shared memory and a mixture-of-experts architecture.
The NPU is designed to run MoE models with up to 30 billion parameters, activating about 3 billion parameters per token according to the report.
Qualcomm said INT4 prefill performance is up to 50% faster and that the NPU is designed for agentic-AI workloads on future premium Snapdragon platforms.
stories.score_reason: The product announcement materially advances mobile AI compute through a new NPU architecture, larger on-chip memory and sparse-model support.

stories.headline: Samsung shares fab-management practices with Korean public nanofabs
bullets: Samsung Electronics provided operating and management practices to the Nanofusion Technology Institute’s public nanofab from March through August.
The work covered safety, chemical handling, cleanroom management, equipment maintenance and preventive maintenance.
The practices are expected to be shared with 14 public nanofabs through the national MoaFab platform.
stories.topic: WFE · Foundry · Materials & Inputs · Supply Chain
stories.score_reason: The programme transfers major-fab operating practices into shared public manufacturing infrastructure, improving Korean semiconductor ecosystem capability.

stories.headline: KB Securities sees hyperscaler free cash flow rebounding from 2028
bullets: KB Securities forecasts hyperscaler free cash flow will begin rebounding in 2028 as cloud utilisation, pricing and margins improve, according to @pequityresearch.
The companies identified in the recap are META, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN and ORCL.
stories.score_reason: Qualifying sell-side model-economics commentary on hyperscaler profitability and cloud utilisation, with a multi-year forecast horizon.

stories.headline: AI datacenter expansion drives a race for large transformers and HVDC equipment
bullets: Economic Daily reports that AI datacenter transformer requirements have risen to at least 150–200MVA, while transformer lead times are commonly two to three years.
TECO is targeting datacenter power projects in the Americas and Southeast Asia and plans an Indonesian transformer plant.
Tatung is developing HVDC and solid-state-transformer technologies and has won 345kV transformer orders in Texas and California.
stories.score_reason: Large-transformer lead times and high-voltage infrastructure are becoming material bottlenecks for AI datacenter deployment.

stories.headline: TSMC and 17 suppliers advertise more than 1,000 jobs in southern Taiwan
bullets: TSMC and 17 suppliers held a joint recruitment event in Kaohsiung offering more than 1,000 engineering, technician and assistant-engineer positions.
TSMC’s Kaohsiung fab chief said the company was mass-producing 2nm technology this year and recruiting local talent to expand production.
Participating suppliers included KLA, Tokyo Electron, ASML, Applied Materials and Lam Research.
stories.score_reason: The event links TSMC’s 2nm ramp with a large regional hiring push involving major equipment suppliers.

stories.headline: OpenAI reportedly will not launch an IPO in 2026
bullets: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Fortune that the company would not launch an initial public offering in 2026, according to AP.
Altman linked the decision to safety, alignment and cooperation between the AI industry and governments.
The report said Anthropic and OpenAI were preparing for possible future public-market debuts that could value them at many hundreds of billions of dollars.
stories.score_reason: The reported IPO timing is a material frontier-AI financing and corporate-strategy development, explicitly linked to safety and alignment priorities.

stories.headline: Powertech and Taiwanese AI-hardware companies prepare investor briefings
bullets: Powertech Technology is scheduled to brief investors on September 15, with memory-industry conditions among the expected topics.
The company previously said memory remained in short supply, customers were maximising wafer output and HBM and standard-memory demand were growing.
AMAX-KY and Hongzhi are also scheduled to brief investors on liquid-cooled AI server shipments, new platforms and high-speed, high-power products.
stories.score_reason: Current investor briefings from a major memory OSAT and AI-server suppliers provide timely read-through on memory tightness and datacenter hardware demand.

stories.headline: Taiwan semiconductor expansion faces a shortage of fab construction workers
bullets: A 2026 semiconductor talent report cited by CTEE says the industry has about 47,000 monthly job openings, up 20% year over year.
Construction and drafting roles have a particularly high labour-demand ratio as TSMC and other companies accelerate fab expansion.
Algorithm-engineer pay rose more than 15.7%, with median annual pay above NT$1.41 million; the report says TSMC is recruiting for 13 plants.
stories.score_reason: The report identifies labour availability as a direct constraint on semiconductor fab expansion and documents rapid growth in AI-related hiring demand.

stories.headline: Anthropic reports Claude use in Iranian-linked military activity
bullets: Anthropic’s threat report said an Iran-linked actor used Claude for naval reconnaissance, targeting recommendations and research into communications vulnerabilities.
The report said a Houthi-linked cell used Claude Code for guidance, navigation, firmware and simulation work related to several missile programmes.
Anthropic said it banned 16 Claude accounts linked to Iranian paramilitary and domestic-security agencies, added detection measures and shared its findings with authorities.
stories.score_reason: Reported frontier-model use in weapons development and surveillance creates significant safety, export-control and national-security implications.

stories.headline: Unofficial mod brings Nvidia Multi Frame Generation to RTX 40-series GPUs
bullets: Tom’s Hardware tested a community mod that enabled Multi Frame Generation beyond its official RTX 50-series support on RTX 40-series cards.
The test found the feature increased perceived smoothness in Cyberpunk 2077, while higher multipliers produced visible artifacts.
The report emphasized that input latency, rather than generated frame rate alone, determines whether the modded experience remains playable.
stories.score_reason: Relevant AI-hardware software development and product-segmentation story, but unofficial, gaming-focused and narrower in industry impact.

stories.headline: ABF substrate demand is adding another constraint beneath AI accelerators
bullets: Tom’s Hardware reported that Ajinomoto’s ABF substrates are critical materials for data-center silicon from Nvidia, Intel and AMD.
The report said demand has strained supply chains and pushed ABF substrate prices up by approximately 30%.
stories.topic: Compute · Advanced Packaging · Substrates · Materials & Inputs · Supply Chain
stories.score_reason: Substrate availability and pricing are material packaging and AI-accelerator bottlenecks, though the evidence is a specialist analysis rather than a company announcement.

stories.headline: GPU-server average price reportedly rose 43.6%; Lenovo led x86 server shipments
bullets: Xinzhixun posts an article reporting a 43.6% increase in average GPU-server prices.
The same headline says Lenovo ranked first in x86 server shipments.
stories.score_reason: Signals strong enterprise AI-server pricing and a notable x86-server shipment ranking, although the covered period is not supplied.

stories.headline: Analyst explains why reused NAND carries more wear risk than reused DRAM
bullets: The Weibo author says normal DRAM reads and writes cause little lifetime wear, with heat, voltage fluctuation, static damage and reballing risks more important for reused parts.
The post says reused NAND has greater risk because program/erase cycles consume the medium; it cites typical endurance of about 3,000 cycles for TLC and 1,000 for QLC.
stories.score_reason: Substantive memory-technology commentary with specific failure mechanisms and endurance claims, presented as technical analysis rather than independently verified research.

weibo_posts.original_text: 聊一下二手拆机存储芯片的问题，圈子里这个也算是公开的秘密了。不谈别的，只聊一下技术。 先说DRAM。正常使用下，DRAM的读写操作本身几乎不消耗寿命；失效大多来自长期高温、电压波动、静电损伤。二手DRAM剩余寿命相对可观；风险更多来自拆机、重新植球带来的虚焊，而非芯片本身的磨损。 再说说NAND。NAND存在PE（Program / Erase）擦写循环上限，每一次写入删除都会损耗介质。TLC原厂典型约3000次PE，QLC约1000次PE。二手颗粒已经消耗一部分PE；同时还有电荷保持能力衰减。 所以说二手NAND影响远大于二手DRAM。

stories.headline: Apple A20 Pro benchmark submission shows major single-thread gains
bullets: An early Geekbench 7 submission attributed to Apple’s A20 Pro showed 4,006 single-thread and 11,460 multi-thread points, according to Tom’s Hardware.
The reported result was 23.3% higher in single-thread and 27.1% higher in multi-thread performance than the cited A19 Pro result.
Tom’s Hardware cautioned that the submission may not represent final retail-product performance; the report also said A20 Pro is built on a 2nm process.
stories.score_reason: Potentially significant mobile-chip performance and process-node development, but evidence is an early benchmark submission and therefore not fully confirmed.

stories.headline: TrendForce data: Nvidia outpaced the combined revenue of fabless ranks two through ten in 2Q26
bullets: The Weibo author, citing TrendForce data, says Nvidia led the 2Q26 global top-10 fabless ranking by more revenue than ranks two through ten combined.
The post says Broadcom ranked second on XPU/ASIC and networking growth; AMD ranked third, with data-center CPU revenue setting a record for a fifth consecutive quarter.

It also says Qualcomm was the only top-10 company with sequential revenue decline, MediaTek's AI-ASIC growth offset weaker mobile chips, and OmniVision was the only mainland fabless company in the ranking.
stories.score_reason: Detailed quarterly fabless ranking commentary highlights the scale of AI infrastructure demand, data-center CPU growth and mobile-chip weakness.

weibo_posts.original_text: TrendForce数据，26Q2全球Top10 Fabless营收排名： 英伟达已经一骑绝尘，比第二到第十的总和还要多。 博通第二，XPU/ASIC+网络芯片业务成为主要推动力。 AMD第三，数据中心CPU营收连续第五个季度创下历史新高。 高通第四，是前10中二季度环比唯一营收减少的厂商。主要是手机芯片的拖累。数据中心业务要到今年四季度才能体现。（高通的收入只包含QCT营收，不含QTL） MTK第五，AI ASIC的增长抵消了手机芯片的下降。 豪威是大陆Fabless唯一入围的厂商。

stories.headline: Jensen Huang says Nvidia gets $100 back for every $1 invested
bullets: Xinzhixun posts an article quoting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as saying, in effect, that Nvidia invests one dollar and receives 100 dollars back.
The headline frames the remark as a response to criticism of circular financing and as an argument for more investment.
stories.score_reason: Relevant commentary on AI infrastructure investment economics, but the supplied evidence is only a headline and does not provide the surrounding context.

bullets: Xinzhixun posts an article reporting that Apple's A20 Pro achieved an approximately 25% performance improvement in testing.
No test platform, baseline or independent confirmation is supplied.
stories.score_reason: Potentially relevant mobile-processor performance news, but the evidence is limited to an unverified article headline.

stories.headline: TSMC proposes a more integrated advanced-packaging development model
bullets: TSMC advanced-packaging executive Kevin Ho proposed system technology co-optimization, or STCO, with standardized and modular platforms linking chip systems, processes, materials and equipment.

The initiative aims to bring suppliers into packaging development earlier as AI-chip cycles accelerate and advanced packages must integrate compute, memory and increasingly photonics while addressing yield, warpage and thermal issues.

The report says TSMC is working through a SEMICON 3DIC alliance with Applied Materials, C Sun, Eternal Materials and Chroma, and plans an advanced-packaging R&D and validation base in Kaohsiung’s Baipu industrial park.
stories.score_reason: Foundry-led packaging ecosystem change addresses a major AI hardware bottleneck and supplier-validation timelines.

stories.headline: Top-10 fabless chip revenue surged 73% in Q2, TrendForce says
bullets: TrendForce reported combined second-quarter revenue of the world’s 10 largest fabless companies at $141.45 billion, up 73% year over year.
Nvidia remained first with $91.16 billion, while Broadcom reached $18.89 billion and AMD moved into third place with $11.53 billion, overtaking Qualcomm.
The report attributed the surge to AI infrastructure demand for GPUs, ASICs, CPUs and high-speed interconnect chips.
stories.score_reason: Large, quantified industry-wide growth shows the scale and breadth of AI-driven chip demand and changes the fabless ranking.

stories.headline: AI compute demand is still reported to exceed infrastructure supply
bullets: A report summarizing takeaways from Goldman Sachs and Citi technology conferences said demand for AI compute, infrastructure and hardware is vastly outpacing supply.
The same summary said several companies saw no slowdown through 2027 and 2028, with cloud-service providers expected to continue increasing capital expenditure next year.
stories.score_reason: Supply-demand imbalance and continued cloud capex are central signals for semiconductor, equipment and AI-infrastructure capacity, but the evidence is a conference recap on X.
